title: Implement deadman switch and tighten fallback heuristics after routing oscillation
creator: Sophie Chen
description:
Summary: During a regional capacity spike on 2026-03-09 we observed repeated cross-region reroutes and an amplified set of fallbacks that increased p99 latency and token cost for affected customers. Root cause: a concurrent policy rollout updated variant preference weights without atomically validating runtime compatibility (quantization/kv-cache compatibility) and left fallback heuristics too eager to select cheaper variants. This produced a feedback loop where failed completions triggered retries, which prioritized other regions and incompatible variants, causing oscillation. Detection: alerts fired from Console latency SLOs and a spike in 'fallback_rate' telemetry; on-call routed the incident to the routing team. Impact: ~3% of requests for a subset of enterprise customers experienced 2–6s additional latency over a 27-minute window; billing and metrics show a token cost delta for those requests. This ticket tracks follow-ups: short-term safeguards deployed, instrumentation gaps filled, medium-term policy and routing algorithm changes, and a long-term rollout gating plan.

Timeline (brief):
- 2026-03-09 14:12 UTC: spike detected in p99 latency; fallback_rate doubled for model-flavor families A/B.
- 14:18 UTC: on-call enabled stricter circuit breakers and throttled cross-region retries (hotfix).
- 14:40 UTC: emergency policy rollback of last deployment removed the inconsistent weight update.
- 15:05 UTC: traffic stabilized but oscillation resumed intermittently as stale caches converged.
- 2026-03-10: post-incident analysis initiated, instrumentation gaps identified.

Key findings:
- Policy rollout race: rolling update changed variant weight matrix while routing controller was concurrently reconciling TTLs; lack of atomicity created a temporary state where preference pointed to incompatible quantized variants.
- Fallback aggressiveness: fallback heuristics preferred cost-lower variants without checking model compatibility, leading to silent degradation and retry amplification.
- Telemetry blind spots: we lacked fine-grained per-variant failure counters and per-route fallback bloom metrics which delayed root cause attribution.
- Missing deadman: routing controller had no short-circuit 'deadman' to stop repeated fallbacks after N unsuccessful handoffs.

This ticket goal: implement a short-term deadman safeguard, tighten fallback selection to validate compatibility, add telemetry, and produce a rollout gating procedure to prevent similar incidents.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Sophie Chen: Initial RCA draft attached. We validated that the policy update changed weights and TTL semantics; the routing controller accepted the new weights but did not validate model execution compatibility. I've uploaded failure traces and heatmaps to the incident Confluence page.

2026-03-11 — Ethan Brooks: Hotfix summary — circuit breaker added to routing-controller: backoff after 3 failed fallbacks within 30s per request-id. This reduced repeat fallbacks in the canary region. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1892

2026-03-12 — Priya Nanduri (SRE): Added dashboard panels for per-variant failure_rate and fallback_count. Observed fallback_count drop after hotfix. Need to retain 30d of this telemetry for regression detection. Refer to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/api/d/xyz/routing-fallbacks

2026-03-13 — Miguel Alvarez (Product): Agreed on rollout gating: all policy weight updates must pass compatibility checks and smoke tests in staging and have a staged rollout with canary traffic at 2% for 30m. Logged as a required policy in the console UI. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood/board/routing/gating-design

2026-03-14 — Sophie Chen: Design decision — we will implement a 'deadman switch' in the routing controller that pauses further fallback attempts for a request-path after 3 unsuccessful variant handoffs in 1 minute. In addition, fallback selection will require a compatibility bit from model-metadata (quantization, kv_cache_schema). Work split into three PRs: (1) telemetry + metrics, (2) controller deadman + backoff, (3) policy rollout gating + UI changes.
